activity_context.topic_title: Linear Independence of Solutions to Homogeneous ODEs

feedback.worked_solution:
The Wronskian $W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})$ of two functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)$ is defined as:

$$
W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})=|\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}^{′} & {y}_{2}^{′}\end{aligned}|={y}_{1}{y}_{2}^{′}-{y}_{2}{y}_{1}^{′}
$$

In our case, we have ${y}_{1}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).$ Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}W({y}_{1},{y}_{2}) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)){(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))}^{′}-(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)){(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))}^{′} \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))-(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)) \\  & =2{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+2{sin}^{2}⁡(2x) \\  & =2({cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2x)) \\  & =2(1) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
